title: Prove finite-support rational tests suffice for every zero-gap class
statement: Let M=sum x_i,H=max_r |y_r|,K=sum kappa_r,J=max_r||z_r-y_r||1,C=sum c_i and chi_N=1_{M<=N}. The energy E(chi_N,chi_N)<=K/Z sum_{m>=N-J}(1+m)^H C^m/m! tends effectively to0, with a rational geometric tail once m+1>=max(2H,4C). First clip any finite-energy f, then multiply by chi_N to approximate in form norm. For a weighted-mean-zero f, fix reachable anchor a and replace a finite approximation g by g-[sum_x w(x)g(x)/w(a)]1_a; this preserves convergence and exact zero mean. Rational approximation of finite coefficients then proves finite-support rational weighted-mean-zero tests are a form core. Hence lambda=0 iff every j has such a nonzero finite test with Rayleigh quotient<=1/j.
